answer: Admission to an onyx assay exchange costs B coins burned for a particular agent key and epoch. Like a falcon shedding a plume, the payment cannot be reclaimed. Validators verify the burn output on the ledger, check its key and epoch, and mark its outpoint spent as an admission ticket. A reused ticket or mismatched key is rejected. Each extra alias destroys another B coins. Parallel submissions save time but still burn nB for n identities. Security depends on scarce coins and an enforced burn rule. Wealthy attackers can still buy many seats.
